insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Base Sum Insured options: ₹1L / ₹2L / ₹3L / ₹4L / ₹5L / ₹7.5L / ₹10L / ₹15L / ₹25L (Policy Schedule will show chosen SI). Re-fill up to 100% of Base SI. Optional I-Protect increases SI by 10% of Base SI each renewal if opted.

great.name: Pre-hospitalization cover: 90 days
great.quote: We will not be liable to pay Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses for more than 90 days immediately preceding the Insured Person’s admission
great.explanation: Covers medical expenses for 90 days before hospitalization (subject to an admissible inpatient/day care/modern treatment/domiciliary claim). This is better than the common 30-60 day limit.

great.name: Built-in additional Sum Insured buffer: Re-fill up to 100% of Base SI (after exhaustion)
great.quote: We will provide a Re-fill amount of maximum up to 100% of the Base Sum Insured
great.explanation: After Base SI (and I-Protect increased SI, if any) is exhausted, an extra buffer up to 100% of Base SI becomes available for subsequent claims in the same policy year (with conditions).

good.name: PED waiting period: 36 months
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 36 months of continuous coverage (standard-good in the market).

good.name: Specific disease/procedure waiting period: 24 months
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.
good.explanation: Listed specific illnesses/procedures are covered after 24 months (industry standard).

good.name: Initial waiting period: 30 days (non-accident)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident
good.explanation: Standard 30-day initial waiting period for illnesses; accidents covered from day 1.

good.name: Post-hospitalization cover: 180 days
good.quote: We will not be liable to pay Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses for more than 180 days immediately following the Insured Person’s discharge from Hospital
good.explanation: Covers follow-up expenses for 180 days after discharge (good, upper end of common market limits).

good.name: Domiciliary hospitalization covered (and Home Health Care services covered with conditions)
good.quote: We will indemnify on a Reimbursement basis the Medical Expenses incurred for Domiciliary Hospitalization... The Home Health Care Services are covered only if We have accepted a claim under Section 3.1 (Inpatient Care) above and Home Health Care Services are availed immediately after that Hospitalization.
good.explanation: Provides home-based treatment coverage when hospitalisation isn’t possible/bed unavailable (domiciliary). Also offers home health care after an accepted inpatient claim, via empanelled providers in selected cities.

bad.name: Room rent limit for ₹1L/₹2L plans: 1% of Base SI per day (daily cap)
bad.quote: Room Rent (per day) Up to 1% of Base Sum Insured
bad.reference: Annexure IV (Product Benefit Table) – Room Rent (per day) for 1 lac / 2 lacs
bad.explanation: A daily room rent cap can reduce claim payouts and can trigger proportionate deductions on the entire bill if you choose a higher category room.

bad.name: Proportionate deduction applies if room category higher than eligibility (impacts total associated medical expenses)
bad.quote: We shall be liable to pay only a pro-rated portion of the total Associated Medical Expenses... in the proportion of the difference between the Room Rent actually incurred and the Room Rent specified in the Policy Schedule
bad.explanation: If you take a room above your eligible limit (relevant especially where room rent is capped like 1% of SI/day), the insurer can reduce payment across associated medical expenses proportionately.

bad.name: Restore/Refill not available for same illness in the same policy year
bad.quote: The re-fill amount may be used for only subsequent claims... and shall not be for any Illness / Injury (including its complications or follow up) for which a claim has been paid or accepted as payable in the current Policy Year for the same Insured Person.
bad.explanation: Refill works only for subsequent claims of a different illness/condition for the same insured in the same year; it cannot be used for a repeat/same illness claim.

bad.name: Consumables not covered (large list of non-payable items incl. gloves, masks, kits etc.)
bad.quote: ANNEXURE II – List I – Expenses not covered... 56 GLOVES ... 60 MASK ... 58 ANY KIT WITH NO DETAILS MENTIONED [DELIVERY KIT, ORTHOKIT, RECOVERY KIT, ETC]
bad.reference: Annexure II (List I – Expenses not covered)
bad.explanation: Many common hospital consumables are excluded, which can create significant out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization.

unclear.name: Co-pay terms (base plan) depend on Policy Schedule; not explicitly stated as 0% by default
unclear.quote: Co-payment (if applicable) as specified in the Policy Schedule shall be applicable on the amount payable by Us.
unclear.explanation: The policy wording defines co-pay as schedule-driven. Verify your Policy Schedule to confirm whether any co-pay applies (and if Zone 2 is chosen, 20% co-pay applies for treatment in Mumbai/Delhi NCR/Kolkata/Gujarat).

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
